summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best videos are about a surprising 'it doesn't see/hear the way you think' idea in sensors and robots (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR motion sensor, IR wall-avoiding robot). Weaker ones are generic 'How does X work?' questions about public places and appliances (lift door, mall door, taps, smoke detectors), which get few views, likes or saves.
winningPattern: A robot or sensor shown as a simple, surprising 'it can't do X, it only does Y' fact, with a bold, short Hindi title in Hinglish (e.g. 'Clap Switch Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Gyro Ke Bina Ye Robot Turant Gir Jaata'). Topics are hobby-friendly (robots, clap switch, PIR, IR, mic) rather than everyday building tech. Posted on Instagram Reels first, with Hindi narration; YouTube works only for a few (clap switch, gyro, PIR at 500-700 views).
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module videos with a 'no brain / can't see / only hears' contradiction hook
Series on the clap switch and robot sensors: the top videos cluster here, and a follow-up can reuse the audience
Lead with a visible robot demo or failure (falling, hitting a wall) in the first second
End with a save or share prompt like 'save this for your next project': robot and IR videos earn the shares and saves
Keep posting Hindi; test one video per week on YouTube with the strongest Instagram topic to learn why YouTube lags
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' titles about public-place gadgets (lift, mall door, tap, smoke alarm)
Posting near-duplicate topics within days (two smoke detector, two IR-in-dark, two tap videos) that split the audience
Mixing in English videos or uploads with no Instagram version: the English Arduino video got 161 YouTube views and zero Instagram
